purpose: How a licensed life insurance agent turns a household or business owner's actual circumstances into a documented, defensible coverage recommendation: running a disclosure-first fact-find, auditing in-force coverage, sizing the need by a named method, establishing a premium the client can sustain for the life of the contract, understanding term and permanent product mechanics well enough to match product class and riders to the objective under the applicable suitability and best-interest standard, presenting illustrations without implying guaranteed performance, handling replacement of existing coverage as a regulated transaction, and carrying the case honestly through application, underwriting, offer variance and policy delivery.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the agent already holds an active life line license and the carrier appointments required to solicit in the client's state; that licensing path is the sibling KB's territory and is treated here only as a precondition to check

product mechanics are described structurally (what drives a price, a charge, a credit or a guarantee) rather than by any specific rate, premium, cash value or commission figure, because those vary by carrier, contract, product generation, jurisdiction and the individual insured

suitability, best-interest, illustration and replacement obligations are named as obligation classes whose current wording, forms and timing must be verified in the agent's own jurisdiction and in each carrier's compliance manual before use
everything here is educational and procedural knowledge for the agent's own practice; it is not personalized financial, insurance, tax, legal or medical advice for any specific consumer
exclusions: the licensing path, pre-licensing and continuing education obligations, and how to obtain or maintain appointments (covered by the licensing and market-focus KB)
captive versus independent versus marketing-organization affiliation, who owns the book, contracting hierarchies, and carrier or product-shelf selection (covered by the licensing and market-focus KB)
choosing a market focus such as young families, business owners or final expense, and lead generation or prospecting ethics (covered by the licensing and market-focus KB)

persistency economics, chargeback and renewal or trail compensation mechanics, service cadence, scheduled policy reviews, referral systems and long-run book building (covered by the persistency and book-building KB)
claims adjudication, death claim filing and beneficiary settlement administration after a loss
personalized financial, investment, tax, legal or estate planning advice to a specific consumer, and any drafting or interpretation of trusts, wills, buy-sell agreements or divorce decrees

any promise, projection presented as a promise, or performance guarantee on cash-value, indexed or variable products, and any invented commission percentage, crediting rate, premium or cash-value figure
medical opinion or interpretation of a client's diagnosis, and any advice to a client about medical treatment or testing
recommending or effecting securities transactions, which require separate registration and licensing outside this subdomain

competency_questions.question: Where does an insurance recommendation end and personalized financial, tax or legal advice begin, and what must I refuse or refer out?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ADVICE_BOUNDARY_FRAME states what the agent may discuss under an insurance license, names the questions that must be referred to a tax, legal or investment professional, and requires the referral and the waiting-on-documents condition to be recorded in the file

competency_questions.question: Which standard of care governs this recommendation, and what has to exist in the file to show I met it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUITABILITY_STANDARD_MAP names the obligation classes (care, disclosure, conflict-of-interest, documentation) and flags jurisdiction verification, and SUITABILITY_DOCUMENTATION lists the artifacts that evidence each one

competency_questions.question: How do I run a first meeting that surfaces true financial facts without pressure or fear-selling, and what must be on the table before any product is named?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISCOVERY_MEETING_FRAME defines the disclosure-first opening and the no-fear-selling constraint, and FACT_FIND_DATA_SET enumerates the fields that must be captured or explicitly declined before a product discussion

competency_questions.question: How do I adapt the process for a client who is grieving, elderly, cognitively impaired, language-limited or being pushed by a third party?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VULNERABLE_CLIENT_CARE gives the observable signals, the slow-down protocol (second meeting, written summary, independent interpreter, trusted contact) and the stop condition when comprehension cannot be established

competency_questions.question: How much coverage does this household actually need, by which method, and what is the gap after everything already in force?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NEED_QUANTIFICATION_METHODS names the method used and its written assumptions, and EXISTING_COVERAGE_AUDIT nets group, individual and employer-provided coverage out of the requirement from policy documents rather than client memory

competency_questions.question: What premium can this client actually sustain for the whole coverage horizon, and which objective wins when the budget cannot fund everything?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BUDGET_AND_AFFORDABILITY produces a stress-tested sustainable premium and GOAL_PRIORITIZATION ranks the competing objectives so the highest-priority need is funded first and the residual gap is recorded

competency_questions.question: How do term and permanent products actually work, and what mechanically moves their cost and their guarantees?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TERM_MECHANICS explains level periods, renewal at attained age and the conversion privilege with its deadline, and PERMANENT_MECHANICS separates guaranteed elements from non-guaranteed elements and names the charges and funding assumptions that decide whether the contract stays in force

competency_questions.question: Which riders genuinely serve this client's stated need, and what does each one cost and require to trigger?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RIDERS_AND_OPTIONS ties each rider to the specific fact-find finding that justifies it and states its trigger definition, cost mechanism and the conditions under which it pays nothing

competency_questions.question: How is my compensation generated by this sale, how does it differ across product classes, and what must I disclose about it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POLICY_COST_STRUCTURE describes compensation as a mechanism driven by product class, target premium definition and the carrier contract without asserting any figure, and states the conflict-of-interest disclosure duty at the point of recommendation

competency_questions.question: Given the sized need, the sustainable premium and the ranked objectives, which product class and structure do I recommend, and how do I show why?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NEED_TO_PRODUCT_MATCH derives the class from need duration and objective rather than from product preference, and SUITABILITY_DOCUMENTATION records the alternatives considered and the reason each was not chosen

competency_questions.question: How do I present a cash-value illustration so the client understands what is guaranteed and what is only a projection?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ILLUSTRATION_DISCIPLINE requires the guaranteed column to be presented and acknowledged first, forbids projection-as-promise and investment-return language, and requires a reduced-assumption scenario alongside the illustrated one

competency_questions.question: When is replacing an existing policy defensible rather than churning, and what has to be disclosed, compared and filed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POLICY_SWITCH_DISCIPLINE puts the burden of proof on the replacement, requires a side-by-side comparison including contestability restart and new charges, and names the replacement notice and form obligations to verify in the jurisdiction and carrier manual

competency_questions.question: How do I complete the application and manage underwriting so the client is never surprised, and what do I do when the offer comes back rated, modified, postponed or declined?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: APPLICATION_INTEGRITY requires full disclosure of every health, tobacco, avocation and financial question with the client reading what they sign, UNDERWRITING_PROCESS explains the evidence pipeline and risk classing, and OFFER_VARIANCE_HANDLING requires a re-fit against need and budget before any changed offer is delivered

competency_questions.question: What must happen at policy delivery, and what has to be in the file before the case leaves the sales process?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DELIVERY_AND_FREE_LOOK requires comparing the issued contract to what was proposed, explaining the right-to-examine period and confirming beneficiaries, and HANDOFF_TO_SERVICE defines the closed-file contents and the review-trigger list passed to the service function

glossary.definition: The structured interview and data capture that records a client's household structure, dependents, income, debts, existing coverage, employer benefits, health and lifestyle history, budget, business interests and stated objectives; it is the evidentiary base for every later recommendation and the thing a complaint file is judged against.

A need-sizing method that estimates the economic value of the insured's future earnings to the household over the working horizon, discounted and net of the insured's own consumption and taxes; it tends to produce a larger requirement than a bucketed needs approach and is sensitive to the earnings and horizon assumptions the agent writes down.

A need-sizing method that adds up specific obligations the death benefit must fund (final expenses, debt payoff, mortgage, income replacement for a stated number of years, education, care for a dependent) and subtracts existing liquid assets and in-force coverage to leave the gap; it can be run as capital liquidation (the fund is spent down) or capital retention (only earnings are used), which materially changes the answer.

A contractual right in many term policies to exchange the term contract for a permanent contract from the same carrier without new evidence of insurability, limited by a conversion deadline (an age or a policy year) and by the menu of permanent products the carrier makes available for conversion at that time; missing the deadline destroys an option that cannot be recreated once health has changed.

The accumulated value inside a permanent contract that the owner may access by surrender, withdrawal or policy loan, distinct from the death benefit; it is reduced by policy charges and surrender charges, and its growth is guaranteed only to the extent the contract's guaranteed elements provide, with anything above that dependent on carrier-declared or index-linked crediting.

The carrier-produced ledger showing how a policy is projected to behave year by year under stated assumptions; it contains guaranteed columns (what the contract must do at maximum charges and minimum crediting) and non-guaranteed columns (what it would do at current or illustrated assumptions), and the non-guaranteed columns are projections, not promises.

The underwriting verdict that prices the contract: a preferred, standard or substandard class derived from medical evidence, family history, build, tobacco use, avocations, driving and financial factors, with substandard offers expressed as table ratings or as flat extras for a temporary hazard; the class assigned determines the actual premium regardless of what was quoted.

The window after policy issue during which the carrier may investigate and rescind or adjust the contract for material misrepresentation on the application; its length and the parallel suicide clause are set by contract and jurisdiction, and its existence is why an inaccurate application harms the beneficiary rather than the agent.

The right-to-examine window after policy delivery during which the owner may return the contract for a refund as defined by the contract and jurisdiction; it is the client's last structural protection against a policy that was misunderstood at the point of sale, and its length and start trigger must be verified rather than assumed.

A sale in which new coverage is purchased while existing coverage is terminated, lapsed, reduced, surrendered or borrowed against; it is a regulated class of transaction carrying notice, comparison, disclosure and filing duties for the agent and the carriers involved, and it restarts contestability and any new surrender charge schedule.

nodes.definition: Fix, before the first client conversation, what an insurance license actually authorizes this agent to do and what it does not. Inside the line: explaining how life products work, gathering the facts, sizing a protection need, recommending a policy class, face amount, premium and riders, and explaining contract terms. Outside the line: telling a client how to invest, what tax treatment their situation will receive, whether a trust or buy-sell agreement should exist or what it should say, how to title assets in a divorce, or what to do about a medical diagnosis. The work unit is the discipline of recognizing the crossing point in real time, naming it out loud, referring the question to the client's tax, legal or investment professional, recording the referral, and holding policy design open until the professional's document exists rather than improvising around it.

included: what the insurance license authorizes the agent to explain and recommend
recognizing and naming a tax, legal, investment or medical question in the moment
referral to the client's own professional and the record of that referral
holding a policy design open until a required legal document exists
excluded: how the license is obtained or maintained
drafting or interpreting trusts, wills, buy-sell agreements or decrees
securities recommendations, which require separate registration

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a regulator, carrier compliance manual or the client's own professional redraws what the agent may address without additional licensing

pros.claim: A stated boundary lets the agent say a clean 'that is your accountant's call' without losing authority or the case
pros.example: a business owner asks how the death benefit will be taxed to the company; the agent explains that tax treatment depends on ownership, beneficiary and notice-and-consent facts, refers it to the client's CPA, and designs the policy after the CPA answers

pros.claim: It prevents a recommendation from being built on a legal structure that does not exist yet
pros.example: declining to bind key-person coverage as buy-sell funding until the attorney-drafted agreement names the funding mechanism

cons.claim: Referring out slows cases and can hand the relationship to another advisor who sells the product themselves
cons.example: a CPA who also holds an insurance license takes over the case while the agent waits for a tax answer

cons.claim: A rigid boundary can read as unhelpful to a client who wanted one place to get answers
cons.example: a widow who wanted plain guidance on what to do with a lump sum hears only a referral and disengages

failure_modes: answering a tax or estate question with confident improvisation because the client expects an answer
designing a policy around an assumed legal document that was never executed
letting an insurance recommendation drift into an investment comparison the agent is not licensed to make
acceptance_tests: the file records every question referred out, to which professional, and whether the answer arrived before the recommendation was finalized
no written or verbal statement in the case asserts a specific tax, legal or investment outcome for this client
revisit_triggers: the client's situation acquires a trust, business entity, divorce or estate dimension mid-case
the agent adds a second license or registration that moves the boundary

nodes.definition: Map the obligation classes that govern a life recommendation before making one, because the standard determines the work, not the other way around. The recurring classes are a care obligation (the recommendation must be based on the client's actual circumstances and objectives, not the agent's inventory), a disclosure obligation (who the agent represents, which carriers, the nature of the compensation and any material conflict), a conflict-of-interest obligation (the agent may not place their own compensation ahead of the client's interest), and a documentation obligation (a reasonable basis must be recorded and reproducible later). Which classes bind, in what wording, under which forms and on what timing varies by jurisdiction, by product type and by carrier compliance manual, so this node's operating rule is to name the class, locate the current authoritative text and forms for the state and product at hand, and verify current requirements in your jurisdiction rather than working from memory or from another state's practice.

included: the care, disclosure, conflict-of-interest and documentation obligation classes
locating the current jurisdiction and carrier-specific requirements and forms before a recommendation
how the standard differs by product type and transaction type
excluded: asserting the specific text, threshold or form number of any state's rule
licensing and appointment mechanics
post-sale servicing obligations

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a regulatory amendment, bulletin or carrier compliance update changes an obligation class, its forms or its timing in a state where the agent writes

pros.claim: Naming the obligation class first makes the required evidence obvious before the work is done rather than after a complaint
pros.example: knowing a documentation obligation applies drives the agent to capture alternatives-considered notes during the recommendation meeting instead of reconstructing them a year later

pros.claim: A verify-the-jurisdiction habit survives multi-state practice and rule changes
pros.example: an agent licensed in three states checks each state's current replacement and best-interest requirements per case instead of applying the home state's process everywhere

cons.claim: The mapping is perishable and costs real time to re-verify per state and product
cons.example: a rule update between two cases in the same month invalidates a form set the agent had just standardized

cons.claim: Treating the standard as a checklist can produce compliant paperwork around a recommendation that still does not fit the client
cons.example: a fully signed suitability form attached to a product chosen before the fact-find was read

failure_modes: applying one state's process to a client in another state
relying on remembered rule wording instead of the current authoritative text
confusing carrier compliance policy with the legal obligation, or assuming one satisfies the other
acceptance_tests: for the state and product at hand, the applicable obligation classes are named and the current requirement source and forms were located for this case
the file shows the recommendation's reasonable basis in terms the applicable standard would recognize
revisit_triggers: a jurisdiction adopts or amends a best-interest, suitability, illustration or replacement rule
a carrier issues a compliance bulletin changing required forms or timing
the agent begins writing a product type or a state not previously covered

nodes.definition: Design the first substantive meeting so that truthful financial and health facts can surface at all. The opening is disclosure-first: who the agent is, which carriers they can and cannot offer, that they are compensated when a policy is placed and how that compensation arises in general terms, and that the meeting may end with no purchase. The body asks permission before entering sensitive territory (income, debts, health, dependents), uses open questions about what the client wants protected rather than closed questions that lead to a product, and explicitly forbids fear-selling: no invented statistics about death, no manufactured urgency, no pressure to sign in the first meeting. The close of the meeting states what happens next and what the client will receive in writing, which is what makes a second meeting normal rather than a retreat.

included: disclosure-first opening covering representation and how compensation arises
permission-based questioning sequence into sensitive facts
the prohibition on fear-selling and manufactured urgency
an explicit next-step and written-summary close
excluded: prospecting, lead sourcing and appointment setting
the content list of the fact-find itself
product presentation, which does not belong in this meeting

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a disclosure obligation changes, or observed second-meeting confusion shows the opening is not landing

pros.claim: Disclosing representation and compensation up front removes the single most damaging late-stage surprise
pros.example: a client who learns at delivery that the agent represents one carrier reacts very differently from one told so in minute two

pros.claim: Permission-based questioning gets accurate income, debt and health answers that a product-first pitch never reaches
pros.example: asking whether it is alright to discuss health history before asking about medications surfaces a prescription the client would otherwise have omitted

cons.claim: A no-pressure frame lengthens the cycle and some genuinely motivated buyers drift away between meetings
cons.example: a young family agrees the need is real, postpones to the second meeting, and a job change pushes it another quarter

cons.claim: Full disclosure of limited carrier access can cost cases to agents who never mention theirs
cons.example: a shopper compares two agents and rewards the one who implied unlimited market access

failure_modes: opening with a product or a quote before any facts are known
using mortality anecdotes or manufactured urgency to compress the decision
skipping the compensation disclosure because the client did not ask
acceptance_tests: the meeting record shows representation and compensation disclosure preceded any product discussion
no urgency device, invented statistic or fear appeal appears in the presentation materials or notes
the client leaves with a stated next step and knows a written summary is coming
revisit_triggers: a disclosure requirement changes in the jurisdiction or carrier manual
clients repeatedly arrive at the second meeting unclear about who the agent represents

nodes.definition: Operate a heightened-care protocol whenever the buyer may not be able to protect their own interests in the transaction. The observable signals include recent bereavement, advanced age combined with confusion or inconsistent answers, cognitive impairment, dependence on a family member or acquaintance who answers for them, limited literacy or a language the agent does not share, severe financial precarity, and any third party who stands to benefit steering the purchase. The protocol slows the process rather than adapting the pitch: schedule a second meeting, provide a plain-language written summary before signature, use an independent interpreter rather than the interested family member, offer a trusted contact where the carrier supports one, verify that the client can restate in their own words what the policy does and what it costs, and stop the sale entirely when comprehension cannot be established or when someone else is driving the decision for their own benefit. Care here is a first-class obligation of the sale, not a courtesy.

included: observable vulnerability signals and how they are recorded
the slow-down protocol: second meeting, plain-language summary, independent interpreter, trusted contact
the comprehension check in the client's own words
the stop condition that ends a sale rather than adapting it
excluded: medical or legal determination of capacity, which the agent is not licensed to make
guardianship, power-of-attorney or elder-law procedure
reporting duties beyond flagging the case to the carrier and following its escalation path

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a senior-protection or trusted-contact requirement changes, or a case review shows a vulnerability signal was missed

pros.claim: A pause protocol prevents the sale that later reads as exploitation of a grieving or impaired buyer
pros.example: a widow three weeks after a funeral is walked through a second meeting and reduces an oversized permanent purchase to coverage she understands and can sustain

pros.claim: Comprehension checks catch misunderstandings that would otherwise surface as free-look cancellations or complaints
pros.example: a client who restates a final expense policy as a savings account reveals the presentation failed before anything is signed

cons.claim: Slowing down loses cases to less careful competitors working the same prospect
cons.example: a senior prospect signs with an agent who closed at the first sitting while this agent scheduled a second meeting

cons.claim: Vulnerability signals are ambiguous and over-reading them can be patronizing to a competent older buyer
cons.example: treating a sharp eighty-year-old business owner as impaired because of age alone

failure_modes: accepting an interested family member as the interpreter and the decision-maker
closing in the first meeting because the client is agreeable rather than because they understood
recording nothing about the vulnerability signals observed, leaving no evidence that care was taken
acceptance_tests: for a flagged case the file records the signals observed, the adaptations made and the comprehension check outcome
no case with an unresolved comprehension failure or third-party pressure was submitted
revisit_triggers: a vulnerability signal appears after the case is already in progress
a carrier or jurisdiction introduces or changes trusted-contact or senior-protection requirements

nodes.definition: Define the concrete data set that must be captured, in writing, before any product can be named. Household and dependants: who relies on this income, their ages, and for how long. Income and stability: sources, whether income is salaried, commissioned or business-derived, and how it would change on a death. Obligations: mortgage balance and term, other debts, education intentions, care obligations for a disabled or aging dependant. Assets and liquidity: what is available to a survivor and how quickly. Existing protection: employer group life, individual policies, association or mortgage coverage. Health and lifestyle: current conditions, medications, family history, tobacco or nicotine use, avocations and travel, and driving record, because these determine whether a quoted price can survive underwriting. Business facts where relevant: ownership share, partners, key employees, existing agreements. Beneficiary intent and any legal documents that bear on it. Objectives in the client's own words. Every field is either captured or explicitly marked as declined by the client, because a blank is indistinguishable later from a question never asked.

included: the household, income, obligation, asset, existing-coverage, health, lifestyle and business fields
beneficiary intent and conflicting legal documents flagged for referral
objectives recorded in the client's own words
explicit marking of any field the client declines to answer
excluded: interpreting medical conditions or prognosis
the need calculation itself
verification of in-force policy detail, which is the audit step

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a client-reported change in health, income, household or objectives, or a carrier adding an underwriting question class the fact-find does not cover

pros.claim: Asking the health, tobacco, avocation and prescription questions during fact-find keeps quoted prices survivable
pros.example: learning about a maintained blood-pressure medication and a recreational pilot licence before quoting prevents a preferred-class quote that underwriting will never honor

pros.claim: Recorded objectives in the client's own words anchor the later suitability rationale
pros.example: the file quotes the client saying the mortgage must be gone and the children must reach eighteen without moving house, which the recommendation then answers point by point

cons.claim: A thorough fact-find is intrusive early and some prospects disengage before its value is visible
cons.example: a prospect who came for a quick quote balks at debt and health questions in the first half hour

cons.claim: Self-reported data is unreliable in exactly the places that matter most
cons.example: a client under-reports drinks per week and over-reports the group life multiple their employer provides

failure_modes: deferring health and lifestyle questions to the application, so the quote and the offer diverge
leaving fields blank rather than marking them declined
collecting facts but never returning to the stated objectives when the recommendation is made
acceptance_tests: every field in the fact-find is populated or explicitly marked declined by the client
health, tobacco, avocation, prescription and driving questions were asked before any premium was quoted
the client's objectives appear as quoted words, not as the agent's paraphrase
revisit_triggers: the client reports a material change in health, income, dependants or debts during the case
a life event or scheduled review reopens the file after handoff

nodes.definition: Inventory what the client already owns from the actual documents rather than from memory, because the gap is defined by this inventory and because any later replacement discussion is judged against it. For each existing contract capture: carrier, product type, face amount, issue date, premium and mode, whether premiums are guaranteed or current-assumption, riders attached, current cash value and any outstanding loan, surrender charge status, contestability status, and for term contracts the level period end date and the conversion deadline and eligible product menu. For employer group coverage capture the multiple provided, what it costs, whether it is portable or convertible on separation, and that it ends with employment. Confirm the beneficiary named on each contract against the client's stated intent, and flag any conflict with a divorce decree, trust or will for referral rather than resolving it. The output is a single in-force schedule that the need calculation nets against.

included: per-contract capture of type, face, riders, cash value, loans and guarantees from documents
term level-period end dates and conversion deadlines and menus
group coverage portability, convertibility and its termination on separation
beneficiary confirmation and flagging conflicts with legal documents
excluded: deciding whether to replace anything, which is a separate regulated analysis
interpreting the legal documents that conflict with a beneficiary designation
servicing or maintaining the in-force policies over time

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an in-force ledger, certificate or carrier statement arrives that contradicts what was recorded from the client's recollection

pros.claim: Netting real in-force coverage out of the requirement prevents recommending a face amount the client does not need
pros.example: a client who believed their group life was two times salary discovers from the certificate it is one times and ends without accidental death coverage

pros.claim: Capturing conversion deadlines surfaces an option that expires silently and cannot be recreated once health changes
pros.example: a ten-year term two years from its conversion deadline gives a newly diagnosed client a permanent option no new application could produce

cons.claim: Clients often cannot produce policies and carriers are slow to release in-force detail, stalling the case
cons.example: waiting on an in-force ledger and conversion menu from a carrier while the client's motivation cools

cons.claim: A thorough audit can reveal that the best action is to keep everything and buy nothing
cons.example: an audit showing adequate group plus an existing convertible term leaves no sale this year

failure_modes: accepting the client's recollection of face amounts and beneficiaries instead of the documents
missing an approaching conversion deadline on an in-force term contract
treating employer group coverage as permanent protection in the gap calculation
acceptance_tests: every in-force contract in the schedule shows type, face, riders, cash value and loan status sourced from a document or carrier statement
term contracts show their level-period end and conversion deadline, and group coverage is flagged as employment-dependent
each beneficiary designation is confirmed against stated intent, with conflicts flagged for referral
revisit_triggers: a policy document or in-force ledger arrives after the analysis was drafted
the client changes employer, which changes the group coverage assumption
a conversion deadline moves within a decision-relevant horizon

nodes.definition: Size the requirement with a named method whose assumptions are written down, because the number is only as defensible as the method behind it. The capital needs approach itemizes what the benefit must fund (final expenses, debt and mortgage payoff, income replacement for a stated number of years, education, ongoing care for a dependant with special needs) and subtracts liquid assets and in-force coverage. The human life value approach values the insured's remaining earnings over the working horizon net of their own consumption. The choice between capital liquidation (the fund is spent to zero over the period) and capital retention (only the fund's earnings are used, preserving principal) changes the answer materially and must be stated. Each assumption the agent supplies (years of income replacement, whether a surviving partner returns to work, education intentions, whether the mortgage is paid off or merely serviced) is recorded next to the number so the client can challenge it and so a reviewer can reproduce it. The output is a requirement, a gap net of the in-force schedule, and a written assumption list; it is never a single number presented as objective fact.

included: capital needs and human life value methods and when each is appropriate
capital liquidation versus capital retention framing
explicit written assumptions attached to the computed requirement
the gap after netting the in-force schedule
excluded: investment return, inflation or tax advice dressed as an assumption the agent asserts as fact
which product will fund the gap, which is the matching step
the premium the client can afford, which is a separate constraint

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the client amends an assumption, or a fact-find input that drives the calculation changes materially

pros.claim: A named method with written assumptions turns a face amount from an opinion into something a client can interrogate
pros.example: a client shortens income replacement from twenty years to twelve because the youngest child will have finished school, and the requirement falls in front of them

pros.claim: Running both a bucketed need and an earnings-based value exposes how wide the defensible range is
pros.example: a household sees a needs-approach figure and a human-life-value figure far apart and chooses deliberately between them

cons.claim: Assumption sensitivity means the method can be steered to produce whatever number the agent wants
cons.example: extending income replacement years and choosing capital retention inflates a requirement toward a larger policy

cons.claim: The computed requirement is frequently unaffordable and can demoralize the client if presented alone
cons.example: a needs analysis produces a figure several times what the household budget can carry, and the client concludes the whole exercise is unrealistic

failure_modes: presenting one number without the method or the assumptions that produced it
quietly selecting the assumption set that maximizes the face amount
forgetting to net in-force and group coverage out of the requirement
acceptance_tests: the file names the method used, lists every assumption supplied by the agent, and shows the gap net of the in-force schedule
the client is recorded as having reviewed and accepted or amended at least the horizon and income-replacement assumptions
revisit_triggers: a fact-find field that feeds the calculation changes
the client challenges or amends an assumption
a life event changes dependants, debts or income

nodes.definition: Establish the premium this household can actually pay for as long as the coverage must last, which is a different question from what they can pay this month. The work: locate the premium inside the client's real cash flow rather than in the space left after an optimistic budget; stress-test it against an income interruption, a rate change on variable debt, and the arrival of a further dependant; distinguish a premium that is fixed and guaranteed for the level period from one that is an assumption requiring ongoing funding; and set the figure jointly with the client so it is theirs, not the agent's. The output is a stated sustainable premium, a note of what was stress-tested, and a stop rule: any design whose required outlay exceeds this figure is not presented as the recommendation, because a policy that lapses in year three leaves the family uninsured, having paid for nothing, at an age and health where replacing it is harder.

included: sustainable premium set against real cash flow, not residual budget
stress tests for income interruption and cost changes
the distinction between a guaranteed level premium and an assumed funding level
the stop rule against presenting an unaffordable design
excluded: household budgeting or debt advice beyond the premium question
the persistency and chargeback economics of a lapse for the agent's book
the product choice itself

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in household income or costs, or an underwriting outcome that pushes the required premium past the stated capacity

pros.claim: A stress-tested premium is the single best predictor that the coverage will still exist when it is needed
pros.example: a household that sets the premium against one income rather than two keeps the policy through a redundancy year

pros.claim: Naming the sustainable premium early kills unaffordable designs before they are ever illustrated
pros.example: the agent never presents a permanent design whose funding requirement exceeds what the couple agreed they could carry

cons.claim: Conservative affordability leaves a real protection gap the client may not appreciate until a claim
cons.example: a family insures the mortgage only, and a death leaves income replacement unfunded

cons.claim: Clients systematically overstate what they can sustain in the enthusiasm of the meeting
cons.example: a couple agrees to a figure they later cut in half when the first annual statement arrives

failure_modes: designing to the need first and discovering affordability only at the illustration
accepting the client's optimistic figure without any stress test
presenting a current-assumption funding level as though it were a fixed premium
acceptance_tests: the file records a client-stated sustainable premium and at least one documented stress test against it
no presented design requires an outlay above that figure without an explicit, recorded client decision to raise it
revisit_triggers: income, employment or household costs change during the case
an underwriting offer raises the required premium above the stated figure
the client asks to reduce premium after the presentation

nodes.definition: Rank the objectives before choosing between them, because a household's stated wants routinely exceed its sustainable premium and the ranking decides what gets funded. The recurring objectives are pure protection for a defined period (children to independence, mortgage to term end), permanence and certainty of a benefit that will pay whenever death occurs (final expense, a lifelong dependant, estate liquidity), business continuity (buy-sell funding, key-person replacement, loan guarantee cover), and cash accumulation inside a contract. The work is to make the client rank these explicitly, to state which are time-bounded and which are lifelong, and to record that ranking in their words, because the ranking is what justifies a term-first recommendation to a client who mentioned savings, or a small permanent policy alongside term for one who wants a burial benefit certain to pay. An unranked objective list produces a compromise product that serves none of them well.

included: eliciting and ranking protection, permanence, business continuity and accumulation objectives
separating time-bounded needs from lifelong needs
recording the ranking in the client's own words as the basis for later tradeoffs
excluded: wealth accumulation or retirement planning advice beyond the insurance contract
the sizing of any individual objective
the product that will serve the ranked objectives

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the client restates or reorders their objectives, or a household change makes a new objective primary

pros.claim: An explicit ranking converts an impossible wish list into a fundable plan with a recorded rationale
pros.example: a couple ranks children-to-independence above a burial benefit, so the budget buys term first and a small permanent policy later

pros.claim: Separating time-bounded from lifelong needs is what actually decides product class
pros.example: identifying a lifelong dependant with special needs turns a term-only conversation into a permanent-coverage conversation on the client's own logic

cons.claim: Clients rank inconsistently under emotion and may revise the order after a single conversation with a relative
cons.example: a client who ranked income replacement first returns wanting only a funeral policy after a family discussion

cons.claim: A ranking exercise can be steered by how the agent frames the options
cons.example: presenting accumulation before protection anchors a client toward a permanent product they did not need

failure_modes: treating an unranked list of wants as a specification and buying a compromise product
letting the agent's preferred product define which objective is described as primary
failing to revisit the ranking when the budget forces a cut
acceptance_tests: the file contains a client-stated ranking of objectives with each marked time-bounded or lifelong
the eventual recommendation can be traced to the top-ranked objectives rather than to the residual ones
revisit_triggers: the client revises what matters most after reflection or family discussion
the budget forces an objective to be dropped or deferred
a new dependant, business interest or lifelong care obligation appears

nodes.definition: Understand term contracts structurally so the recommendation and the client conversation rest on mechanism rather than on a rate sheet. A level term contract guarantees a stated premium for a stated period; at the end of that period most contracts continue but at annually increasing attained-age rates that rise steeply, which is why the level period must be matched to the need's horizon rather than to the cheapest quote. Annual renewable structures start lower and climb every year from the outset. Price is driven by the insured's age at issue, the underwriting class assigned, the face amount, the length of the level period, tobacco or nicotine status, and any riders attached; face amount bands mean a larger policy can cost less per unit than a smaller one. The conversion privilege is the structurally important feature: the right to exchange for a permanent contract without new evidence of insurability, bounded by a deadline and by the carrier's conversion product menu at that time. There is no cash value; the contract pays on death within the period and otherwise expires.

included: level period, post-level attained-age renewal and annual renewable structures
the mechanical drivers of price including age, class, face, term length and nicotine status
the conversion privilege, its deadline and its product menu
the absence of cash value and what expiry means
excluded: any specific premium, rate or price figure
which carrier's term contract to use, which is a product-shelf question
the decision of whether term fits this client, which is the matching step

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier changes term product structure, conversion terms or underwriting class definitions

pros.claim: Matching the level period to the need horizon is a mechanism the client can verify for themselves
pros.example: aligning the level period with the years remaining until the youngest child finishes education, rather than to a round number

pros.claim: Understanding face-amount banding lets the agent show where more coverage costs less per unit
pros.example: a client discovers a higher face lands in a better band and costs little more in total than the amount they first asked for

cons.claim: Term expires exactly when insurability has usually deteriorated, leaving a client uninsurable and uncovered
cons.example: a level period ending at sixty-five for a client who developed a chronic condition at sixty

cons.claim: Post-level renewal pricing is misunderstood by clients as a continuation of the same premium
cons.example: a client who expected the policy to simply continue receives a renewal notice at attained-age rates and lapses it

failure_modes: selling the cheapest level period rather than the one that matches the need horizon
leaving the conversion deadline unexplained and unrecorded
describing post-level continuation without explaining that the premium changes structurally
acceptance_tests: the recommendation states why the chosen level period matches the need horizon
the conversion deadline and its constraints are explained to the client and recorded in the file
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes its conversion menu, deadline or post-level structure
the client's need horizon changes so the level period no longer matches

nodes.definition: Understand permanent contracts as machines with guaranteed and non-guaranteed parts, because everything that goes wrong in this product class comes from confusing the two. The guaranteed part is what the contract must do at its maximum charges and minimum credited rate: a guaranteed premium and guaranteed values in a whole life contract, a guaranteed minimum crediting rate and maximum cost-of-insurance charges in a universal life contract. The non-guaranteed part is everything the carrier currently declares or the index currently produces: dividends on a participating contract, current crediting rates, and in indexed designs the caps, participation rates and floors the carrier may change within contractual limits. Charges are mechanisms too: cost of insurance rising with attained age, policy and administrative charges, premium loads, and surrender charges that decline over a schedule. A universal life contract is funded, not merely paid: if actual crediting and charges differ from the assumptions, the required funding changes and an underfunded contract can lapse decades in, destroying the coverage it was bought for. Nothing in this class is described to a client as a return, a yield or a promise.

included: guaranteed versus non-guaranteed elements in whole life, universal life and indexed designs
cost of insurance, policy charges, loads and surrender charge schedules as mechanisms
funding as an ongoing obligation and the lapse pathway when assumptions miss
cash value access by surrender, withdrawal or loan and its effect on the death benefit
excluded: any projected or asserted crediting rate, dividend, cash value or return figure
variable products requiring securities registration to recommend
tax treatment of policy loans, withdrawals or transfers, which is referred out

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier changes charge scales, crediting parameters or dividend practice, or a product generation alters guaranteed elements

pros.claim: Separating guaranteed from non-guaranteed elements gives the client a floor they can actually rely on
pros.example: a client choosing a design whose guaranteed premium and guaranteed values alone satisfy the final expense objective, with dividends treated as upside only

pros.claim: Treating the contract as funded rather than paid exposes the lapse pathway before it happens
pros.example: showing that a universal life design carried at the minimum illustrated funding may require more money later if crediting falls

cons.claim: The complexity is genuinely hard to convey and clients frequently retain only the attractive half
cons.example: a client who remembers the accumulation story but not the charge structure or the funding obligation

cons.claim: Higher cost per unit of death benefit means a permanent design can crowd out the protection amount the family actually needs
cons.example: a household affording a small permanent face when the same premium would have bought several times the coverage in term during the child-raising years

failure_modes: presenting non-guaranteed elements as though they were contractual
using investment vocabulary such as return or yield for a crediting mechanism
designing at minimum funding without explaining the later funding obligation
acceptance_tests: the client is shown the guaranteed structure separately and can restate what is guaranteed and what is not
any design is checked against the guaranteed-assumption scenario before it is recommended
no material describing the product uses return, yield or investment-performance language
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes cost-of-insurance scales, caps, participation rates or dividend practice
an in-force review shows funding drifting from the design assumption
a new product generation changes the guaranteed structure the agent relies on

nodes.definition: Attach riders only where a specific fact-find finding justifies them, and explain each as a trigger plus a cost rather than as a free feature. Waiver of premium answers an income-interruption risk and turns on a contractual disability definition that must be read, not assumed. Accelerated death benefit riders for terminal, chronic or critical illness advance part of the death benefit on a defined trigger and reduce what the beneficiary receives, which the client must understand before it is described as a living benefit. Guaranteed insurability options buy the right to add coverage later without evidence of insurability, which matters for a young insured whose need will grow. Child and spouse riders cover dependants cheaply but in small amounts and end at defined ages. Return-of-premium structures change the product's cost and cash-flow character rather than adding protection. Term riders on a permanent chassis blend a lifelong base with temporary coverage at lower cost per unit. For each rider the agent records the finding it answers, its trigger definition, how its cost arises, and the circumstances in which it pays nothing.

included: waiver of premium, accelerated benefit, guaranteed insurability, child and spouse, return of premium and term riders
the fact-find finding each rider answers
trigger definitions, cost mechanisms and the circumstances of non-payment
excluded: any specific rider charge or premium figure
long-term care contracts sold as standalone products
medical judgement about whether a client will meet a health trigger

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier revises rider definitions, triggers or availability, or a client circumstance makes a previously declined rider relevant

pros.claim: Tying each rider to a recorded finding stops rider stacking that inflates premium without adding relevant protection
pros.example: declining a critical illness rider for a client whose stated objective is purely a mortgage payoff, and documenting why

pros.claim: A guaranteed insurability option preserves future access for an insured whose need will grow before their health does
pros.example: a newly qualified professional in their twenties who expects children and a mortgage within the decade

cons.claim: Riders complicate the contract and clients often cannot recall what they bought or what triggers it
cons.example: a client who believes an accelerated benefit rider is a separate pot of money rather than an advance of the death benefit

cons.claim: Each rider adds cost that competes with face amount inside a fixed premium
cons.example: rider charges reducing the affordable face amount below the calculated protection gap

failure_modes: adding riders by habit or by carrier default rather than by finding
describing an accelerated benefit as extra money rather than an advance that reduces the death benefit
not reading the disability or illness definition that governs whether the rider ever pays
acceptance_tests: every attached rider names the fact-find finding it answers and its trigger definition in the file
the client can restate what each rider does and what it reduces or costs
riders declined are recorded with the reason they were not appropriate
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes a rider definition, availability or charge structure
the client's circumstances change so a declined rider becomes relevant

nodes.definition: Understand and disclose how this sale pays the agent, because the conflict is structural and pretending otherwise is what turns it into misconduct. The mechanism: first-year compensation is generally computed as a percentage of a defined premium base (a target or first-year premium the carrier defines per product), so the amount varies with product class, with the premium the client pays, with the carrier's contract, and with the agent's contract level; premium paid above the defined base typically compensates at a much lower rate; subsequent-year compensation follows a separate schedule. The consequences to hold in view: a permanent design and a term design serving the same client generate materially different compensation, and so do two permanent designs funded differently. The agent's duty is to know the mechanism for the products they present, never to invent or quote a figure they have not verified in their own carrier contract, and to disclose the existence and nature of the conflict at the point of recommendation in the manner the applicable disclosure obligation requires. No number is stated to a client that the agent cannot show in a contract or schedule.

included: how first-year and subsequent compensation is generated as a mechanism
why product class and funding level change the agent's compensation
the conflict-of-interest disclosure duty at the point of recommendation
verifying compensation terms in the agent's own carrier contract rather than by rumor
excluded: any specific commission percentage, dollar amount or comparison figure
chargeback, renewal and trail economics over the life of the book
contract-level negotiation and hierarchy structure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier compensation schedule or premium-base definition changes, or a compensation-disclosure obligation is amended

pros.claim: Knowing the mechanism lets the agent recognize their own bias before it shapes a recommendation
pros.example: an agent notices that the design they instinctively reached for is the one with the larger premium base and re-tests it against the client's ranked objectives

pros.claim: Proactive conflict disclosure is far cheaper than a client discovering the incentive later
pros.example: telling a client that a permanent recommendation compensates differently than a term one, and then showing why the permanent design answers their lifelong objective

cons.claim: Compensation disclosure can derail a technically correct recommendation by making the client suspicious of it
cons.example: a client rejects an appropriate permanent policy for a lifelong dependant purely because it pays the agent more

cons.claim: The mechanism is genuinely complicated and a partial explanation can mislead as much as silence
cons.example: explaining first-year compensation without mentioning that premium above the defined base compensates differently

failure_modes: quoting a compensation figure from memory or from another agent's contract
letting the higher-compensating design lead the presentation order
treating disclosure as satisfied by a signature on a form the client did not read
acceptance_tests: the compensation mechanism for each presented product is verified against the agent's own carrier contract before the meeting
the conflict disclosure required by the applicable standard is delivered and evidenced at the recommendation
no compensation figure appears anywhere in the case that cannot be shown in a contract or schedule
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes its compensation schedule or premium-base definition
a disclosure obligation about compensation changes in a state where the agent writes

nodes.definition: Derive the recommendation from the need's duration, the ranked objectives and the sustainable premium, in that order, and only then name a product. The core logic: a need with a defined end date (children to independence, a mortgage term, a business loan) is a term need; a need that exists whenever death occurs (final expenses, a lifelong dependant, estate liquidity, a buy-sell obligation that has no end date) is a permanent need; a household with both usually needs both, often as a laddered term structure carrying the temporary load alongside a smaller permanent base. Where the sustainable premium cannot fund the ideal structure, the rule is to fund the top-ranked objective completely rather than every objective partially, and to record the residual gap as a known, client-acknowledged shortfall to revisit rather than hiding it. The recommendation states face amount, product class, level period or funding level, riders, and at least one alternative that was considered and why it was not chosen. A recommendation that cannot be traced back to a fact-find finding and a ranked objective is not a recommendation, it is a preference.

included: duration-of-need logic driving product class
blended and laddered structures where both need types exist
the fund-the-top-objective rule when the premium cannot cover everything
recording alternatives considered and the residual gap
excluded: carrier selection and product-shelf comparison across the market
the illustration presentation itself
the replacement analysis for existing coverage

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in the sized need, the objective ranking, the sustainable premium or the underwriting offer invalidates the derivation

pros.claim: Deriving class from need duration produces recommendations that survive a later challenge
pros.example: a reviewer can follow the file from a lifelong dependant finding to a permanent base plus laddered term without any leap

pros.claim: Funding the top objective completely beats spreading a thin premium across every want
pros.example: buying enough term to carry the children to independence rather than a token amount of everything

cons.claim: Duration logic underweights genuine client preferences such as wanting a paid-up contract they can see
cons.example: a client who values a guaranteed lifelong benefit more than the larger temporary face the same premium would buy

cons.claim: A blended structure is harder to explain and to service than a single contract
cons.example: a client with a permanent base and two term layers who cannot recall which policy covers what

failure_modes: naming the product before the need duration and ranking are established
spreading an inadequate premium across every objective so none is truly covered
leaving the residual gap unstated so the client believes they are fully covered
acceptance_tests: every element of the recommendation traces to a recorded fact-find finding and a ranked objective
at least one alternative structure is documented with the reason it was not chosen
any residual protection gap is stated in writing and acknowledged by the client
revisit_triggers: an underwriting offer changes the price of the recommended structure
the client reorders objectives or changes the sustainable premium
the in-force audit is corrected after the recommendation was drafted

nodes.definition: Assemble the file that will have to speak for the agent years later, when memory is gone and only paper remains. It contains: the completed fact-find with declined fields marked; the in-force schedule and its document sources; the need calculation with its named method and written assumptions; the client-stated sustainable premium and its stress test; the ranked objectives in the client's words; the recommendation with face, class, structure and riders; the alternatives considered and why each was not chosen; the disclosures delivered and when, including representation and compensation conflict; any replacement comparison and forms; the illustration set delivered with the guaranteed columns; and any vulnerability adaptations or referrals made. The discipline is to write each element while the reasoning is live rather than reconstructing it under a complaint, and to make the file legible to someone who was not in the room. A signed form proves a signature; a reasoned file proves a recommendation.

included: the full contents list of a defensible recommendation file
contemporaneous authorship of the reasoning, not reconstruction
legibility to a reviewer who was not present
evidence of disclosures, adaptations and referrals
excluded: record retention periods and storage rules, which are jurisdiction and carrier specific and must be verified
the carrier's own new-business forms processing
post-sale service records, which belong to the servicing function

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a documentation or record obligation changes, or a case event makes the filed rationale no longer accurate

pros.claim: A contemporaneous file is the only durable defense when a recommendation is questioned years later
pros.example: a beneficiary dispute is resolved by notes showing the client chose a smaller face against advice and acknowledged the gap

pros.claim: Writing the rationale while it is live exposes weak reasoning before the case is submitted
pros.example: an agent drafting the alternatives section realizes the chosen structure does not answer the top-ranked objective

cons.claim: Documentation load competes directly with selling time and is the first thing dropped when volume rises
cons.example: an agent with a busy month writes files retrospectively and loses the detail that mattered

cons.claim: A file can be complete and still be a rationalization written after the product was chosen
cons.example: alternatives listed only to be dismissed in a sentence each, with no evidence they were seriously considered

failure_modes: signature-collecting instead of reasoning-recording
reconstructing the rationale after a complaint arrives
omitting the disclosures and adaptations that show how the client was treated
acceptance_tests: the file contains every listed element and a reviewer who was not present can follow the reasoning end to end
every rationale element is dated at or near the meeting it describes rather than after submission
disclosures, replacement forms, illustration sets and any vulnerability adaptations are evidenced in the file
revisit_triggers: a documentation obligation changes in a jurisdiction or carrier manual
an offer variance, delivery issue or client change alters the recommendation after the file was built

nodes.definition: Present illustrations so that the client's decision rests on what the contract must do, not on what it might do. The order is fixed: show and explain the guaranteed columns first, establish that the purchase decision is being made on those values, and only then show the non-guaranteed columns clearly labelled as projections that depend on carrier-declared or index-linked elements which can change. Show a reduced-assumption scenario alongside the illustrated one so the client sees the shape of the downside, and never present a single mid-range projection as the expected outcome. Language discipline is part of the mechanism: no return, yield, interest earned or investment-performance framing for a crediting mechanism, no comparison of a policy to a savings or retirement account, and no page extracted from a ledger without the accompanying guaranteed page. Deliver the complete illustration in the form and at the time the applicable illustration obligation requires, obtain the acknowledgement it requires, and record what was presented, because a client who later re-reads the ledger must find nothing they were not told.

included: guaranteed-column-first presentation order and the decision basis
labelling non-guaranteed columns as projections with changeable inputs
a reduced-assumption scenario shown beside the illustrated one
prohibited investment-performance language and cherry-picked pages
delivery, acknowledgement and recording of the illustration set
excluded: asserting any crediting rate, dividend, cash value or accumulation figure
producing the illustration software output itself
tax treatment of policy values, which is referred out

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier revises illustrated assumptions or ledger format, or an illustration disclosure obligation changes

pros.claim: A guaranteed-first order makes the buy decision robust to every future assumption change
pros.example: a client who bought on guaranteed values is unshaken when the carrier reduces its dividend scale

pros.claim: Showing a reduced-assumption scenario prevents the delivery-stage argument about what was promised
pros.example: the client recognizes a lower-crediting outcome as one they were shown, rather than as a betrayal

cons.claim: Guaranteed columns make a permanent product look unattractive next to a competitor's optimistic presentation
cons.example: a prospect compares an honest guaranteed-first presentation to a rival ledger shown at illustrated values and thinks this agent's product is worse

cons.claim: The full illustration set is long and clients disengage from the very pages that protect them
cons.example: a client signs the acknowledgement without reading the guaranteed page they were walked through

failure_modes: leading with the illustrated column and treating guarantees as a footnote
extracting a favorable ledger page without its guaranteed counterpart
using return or yield language that reframes insurance as an investment
acceptance_tests: the file records that guaranteed values were presented first and that the client acknowledged the buy decision rests on them
a reduced-assumption scenario accompanies every non-guaranteed presentation
no presented material contains investment-return framing or an isolated non-guaranteed page
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes illustrated assumptions, crediting parameters or dividend scale
an illustration obligation or required acknowledgement changes in the jurisdiction
the client asks what the policy will be worth at a future date

nodes.definition: Treat any transaction that terminates, lapses, reduces, surrenders or borrows against existing coverage to fund new coverage as a regulated replacement, with the burden of proof on the replacement rather than on keeping what exists. The analysis compares old and new side by side on: current and future cost, guaranteed elements on each side, the surrender charge and cash value consequence of leaving the old contract, the loss of the old contract's incontestability and its restart on the new one, the suicide clause restart, the client's current health and whether the new policy is actually issued before the old one is touched, any rider or conversion right that is destroyed, and the true reason the client wants the change. Legitimate replacements exist: a genuinely underfunded contract heading to lapse, a materially better structure for a changed need, a carrier problem. Churning is the replacement that serves the new commission. The compliance layer is a class of notice, comparison, signature and carrier-filing obligations whose current forms, timing and definitions must be verified in the jurisdiction and in each carrier's manual before the application is taken, and the old policy is never cancelled until the new coverage is in force.

included: what counts as a replacement transaction including loans and reductions
the side-by-side comparison and the burden of proof on the replacement
contestability and suicide clause restart and destroyed rights
notice, comparison and filing obligation classes to verify per jurisdiction and carrier
the never-cancel-before-in-force rule
excluded: internal carrier exchanges handled entirely as a service transaction with no new underwriting
tax consequences of surrender or exchange, which are referred to the client's tax professional
the persistency and chargeback consequences for the agent's own book

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a replacement regulation, notice form or carrier filing requirement changes, or new in-force data alters the comparison

pros.claim: Putting the burden of proof on the replacement stops the easiest form of self-serving advice
pros.example: an agent declines to replace a healthy in-force contract because the comparison shows only the new commission improves

pros.claim: Surfacing contestability restart converts an abstract compliance point into a concrete client risk
pros.example: a client with a changed health history understands that a fresh contestability window puts the benefit at risk in a way the old contract no longer does

cons.claim: The comparison work and forms are heavy enough that agents avoid legitimate replacements clients would benefit from
cons.example: leaving a client in an underfunded contract drifting toward lapse because the replacement process is onerous

cons.claim: A truthful comparison is genuinely hard when the old contract's in-force data is slow to obtain
cons.example: the old carrier's in-force ledger arrives after the new application deadline the client wanted to meet

failure_modes: cancelling or lapsing the old policy before the new coverage is issued and in force
treating a policy loan or a face reduction as though it were not a replacement
completing the forms without performing the comparison they attest to
acceptance_tests: a documented side-by-side comparison exists covering cost, guarantees, surrender consequence, contestability restart and destroyed rights
the applicable replacement notices and forms for the jurisdiction and carriers were located, completed and filed on the required timing
the old coverage remained in force until the new contract was issued and delivered
revisit_triggers: a replacement rule, form or timing requirement changes in a jurisdiction where the agent writes
in-force data arrives that changes the comparison after it was drafted
the client's health changes between application and delivery

nodes.definition: Complete the application so that what the carrier underwrites is what is true, because every shortcut here transfers risk from the agent to the beneficiary. The rules are unglamorous and absolute: every health, medication, tobacco and nicotine, avocation, travel, driving, criminal and financial question is answered fully; nothing is omitted because the agent judges it immaterial; no answer is written for the client that the client has not stated; the client reads what they sign, including any question the agent asked verbally, and signs no blank or partially completed form. The agent's own statement on the application is answered truthfully, including whether a replacement is involved. Where an answer needs detail, the detail goes in rather than a bare yes. The authorizations required for medical and prescription evidence are explained rather than merely signed. The reason this is a first-class work unit is the contestability period: a misstatement discovered after a death within that window can cost the family the benefit entirely, which is a harm the agent caused and cannot repair.

included: full and detailed answers to every application question class
the client reading and attesting to what they sign, with no blank forms
the agent statement including replacement disclosure
explaining the medical and prescription authorizations
the contestability consequence of any misstatement
excluded: predicting or promising an underwriting outcome
medical interpretation of a disclosed condition
carrier-side new-business processing and requirement ordering

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new material client fact emerges, or a carrier changes its application questions, authorizations or agent statement

pros.claim: A fully disclosed application makes the issued contract as strong as it can be for the beneficiary
pros.example: a disclosed and detailed cardiac history produces a rated offer that pays cleanly at claim rather than an approval that is contested

pros.claim: Detail in the answers reduces underwriting cycles and surprise requirements
pros.example: attaching the specifics of a resolved condition up front avoids an attending physician statement request that adds weeks

cons.claim: Full disclosure produces worse offers and lost cases against competitors who were less thorough
cons.example: a client rated for a disclosed condition sees a cheaper approval from an agent who never asked the question

cons.claim: Thorough applications take longer and clients experience the process as intrusive
cons.example: a client irritated by detailed follow-up questions about a decade-old condition

failure_modes: omitting or softening a disclosure to protect a quoted price
letting a client sign a form the agent completed and they never read
answering the replacement question inaccurately on the agent statement
acceptance_tests: no application question is unanswered, and every affirmative answer carries the detail the carrier requires
the client attests they read every answer, and no blank or agent-completed unread form is signed
the agent statement and any replacement disclosure match the facts of the case
revisit_triggers: the client discloses a new material fact after the application is signed
a carrier changes its application question set or authorization requirements
underwriting surfaces evidence inconsistent with an application answer

nodes.definition: Manage the underwriting pipeline as a process with known stages, evidence types and tradeoffs rather than as a black box the case disappears into. Path choice matters: a fully underwritten path uses the most evidence and generally produces the finest pricing; accelerated or simplified paths trade evidence for speed and convenience with different acceptance boundaries; guaranteed-issue style products accept nearly everyone but structure the benefit accordingly, which is why they are an answer for the uninsurable rather than a default. The evidence set can include a paramedical exam with fluids, attending physician statements, prescription and medical-information databases, motor vehicle records and financial documentation, each with its own turnaround. Financial underwriting independently tests whether the face amount is justified by the economic loss, which is why an oversized request stalls regardless of health. The agent's operating job is expectation-setting at application, a status cadence with the client and the carrier, chasing the specific outstanding requirement rather than the case generally, and knowing when an informal inquiry to a different carrier is the right move before a formal declination exists on record.

included: fully underwritten, accelerated, simplified and guaranteed-issue path tradeoffs
the evidence types and what each is for
financial underwriting of the face amount
status cadence, requirement chasing and informal inquiry before a formal declination
excluded: carrier underwriting guidelines as asserted thresholds, which vary and must be checked per carrier
medical interpretation of results
predicting a specific class or price for a given client

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier changes underwriting programs, evidence requirements or accelerated-path eligibility

pros.claim: Knowing the evidence path lets the agent set expectations that survive a long or intrusive process
pros.example: telling a client at application that a physician statement can add weeks prevents the mid-process assumption that the case was forgotten

pros.claim: An informal inquiry can find a home for a difficult risk without creating a declination on record
pros.example: shopping an impaired risk informally before submitting anywhere formally

cons.claim: Underwriting timelines are largely outside the agent's control and long cases lose clients
cons.example: a case waiting on records from a former physician while the client's interest and health both drift

cons.claim: Accelerated paths that feel client-friendly can misprice or decline a risk a full path would have accepted
cons.example: an algorithmic accelerated decision declining a case that full evidence would have rated modestly

failure_modes: leaving the client without status updates during a long evidence cycle
submitting formally to a carrier likely to decline instead of inquiring informally first
assuming the applied-for class will be the offered class when quoting
acceptance_tests: the client was told at application what evidence the path requires and roughly how it proceeds
every outstanding requirement is tracked by name with a follow-up owner and date
no quoted premium was presented as final before the class was actually offered
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes its underwriting program, evidence rules or accelerated eligibility
an evidence item returns something inconsistent with the application
the case exceeds its expected cycle time

nodes.definition: Treat any offer that differs from what was applied for as a re-opening of the recommendation, not as a paperwork step. The variance types each have their own response: a rated or table offer raises the premium and must be re-tested against the stated sustainable premium and the ranked objectives before it is presented; a modified offer with an exclusion rider, a reduced face or a graded benefit changes what the client is actually buying and must be explained in those terms; a postponement has a defined revisit condition and a plan for the interim; a declination requires knowing whether it is on record, what alternatives exist including guaranteed-issue structures for the genuinely uninsurable, and whether an informal approach to another carrier is appropriate. Where evidence explains the rating (a resolved condition, a controlled result, an outdated record), a reconsideration request with the supporting evidence is legitimate work. What is never acceptable is quietly delivering a policy priced or structured differently from what the client agreed to and hoping the difference goes unnoticed.
